topic: Texas market reality check: days on market, quiet price cuts, concessions
hook: The 37 day shift nobody priced in yet

scores.worst_problem: The hook leans on a stat-plus-vague-authority formula ('nobody priced in yet') that a skeptical scroller can pattern-match to generic market-update content, so the curiosity gap is narrower than the specific number suggests.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 1 to withhold the consequence rather than the metric — e.g. name what the 37 days quietly costs a seller without naming the number — and tighten the slide 5 loop to under six words so the loop cadence stays uniform.

deck.topic: Texas market reality check: days on market, quiet price cuts, concessions
deck.hook: The 37 day shift nobody priced in yet

points.title: The 37 Day Number
body: Homes that sold in a weekend two years ago now average about 37 days across most Texas metros.
Nothing broke. The clock just went back to normal.

points.title: Price Cuts Are Quiet
body: Roughly a third of active listings have already taken a reduction.
You never see it. It just shows up as a new number one Tuesday morning.

points.title: Inventory Nobody Counts
body: Finished new construction sitting empty competes directly with your resale listing.
It does not show up in the numbers most people quote you.

points.title: Concessions Beat Price
body: Sellers are covering closing costs and buying rates down instead of slashing the sticker.
Buyers who ask get help. Buyers who assume get nothing.
points.loop: There is a window for asking.

points.title: The 90 Day Trap
body: Past 90 days on market, buyers stop asking about the house and start asking what is wrong with it.
Pulling it and relisting does not erase the history anymore.
points.loop: Most of this is fixable in a week.

linkedinCaption:
Texas homes are averaging roughly 37 days on market across most metros. Two years ago that was a weekend. Nothing broke. The clock simply went back to where it used to sit.

What gets missed is everything happening underneath that number. About a third of active listings have already taken a reduction, and those cuts are quiet. Finished new construction sitting empty competes directly with resale inventory and rarely shows up in the stats people quote. Sellers are leaning on concessions and rate buydowns instead of dropping the sticker price. Buyers who ask receive help. Buyers who assume receive nothing.

Past 90 days, the conversation shifts from the house to what is wrong with it.

Are you seeing concessions outperform price reductions in your market?
